crisis.title: You don't have to sit with this alone

phq9.label: PHQ-9 (low mood)
phq9.prompt: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following?

items.0: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
items.2: Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
items.3: Feeling tired or having little energy
items.5: Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
items.6: Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
items.7: Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed — or the opposite, being fidgety or restless
items.8: Thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself in some way

gad7.label: GAD-7 (anxiety)
gad7.prompt: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following?

items.0: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
items.1: Not being able to stop or control worrying
items.2: Worrying too much about different things
items.4: Being so restless that it is hard to sit still
items.6: Feeling afraid, as if something awful might happen

landing.heroTitle: A quieter place to check in with yourself.
landing.heroBody: Kalm is a wellness support companion — AI conversation, mood tracking and guided exercises, built around what you tell it about your life.

companion.title: A companion that remembers
companion.body: Your self-introduction, goals and recent check-ins shape every conversation from the first message.

tracking.title: Gentle tracking
tracking.body: Mood and habit check-ins that surface patterns — never streak guilt or shame nudges.

practice.title: Guided practice
practice.body: Short CBT reframes, grounding and journaling flows you can finish in a few quiet minutes.

landing.supportBody: Kalm is a wellness support tool. It is not therapy, not a diagnosis, and not an emergency service. Every conversation is screened for crisis language, and crisis resources are always one tap away and never behind a paywall.

notMedicalCare.heading: Kalm is not medical care
notMedicalCare.body: Kalm is a wellness support tool. It does not diagnose, treat, or provide medical advice, and it is not a replacement for therapy, psychiatric care, or emergency services. If you are in crisis, use the crisis resources page or your local emergency number.

howAiWorks.heading: How the AI works
howAiWorks.body: Conversations are generated by a large language model using the self-introduction and check-in data you choose to share. Every input is screened for crisis language before a normal reply is generated; when crisis language is detected, Kalm interrupts the conversation and shows support resources instead.

yourData.heading: Your data
yourData.body: Mental health information is sensitive personal data. Kalm stores your profile, check-ins, conversations and session transcripts so your experience stays continuous. You can export or delete your data at any time from Profile settings, with no retention dark patterns.

ageRequirement.heading: Age requirement
ageRequirement.body: Kalm is for people aged 13 and over. Teen mode applies stricter safety guardrails and age-appropriate content. Kalm is not intended for children under 13.

workplaceAccounts.heading: Workplace accounts
workplaceAccounts.body: If you access Kalm through an employer plan, your employer can only ever see aggregate, anonymized usage statistics. Your conversations, check-ins and session content are never shared with them.

crisisPage.title: You don't have to handle this alone
crisisPage.body: If you're thinking about harming yourself or someone else, or you're in immediate danger, please reach a real person now. These services are free, confidential, and staffed by trained humans.

lifeline.title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (US)
lifeline.detail: Call or text 988 — 24/7, free and confidential.

textLine.title: Crisis Text Line (US, UK, CA, IE)
textLine.detail: Text HOME to 741741 to reach a trained crisis counselor.

findAHelpline.title: Find a line in your country

crisisPage.immediateDangerTitle: If there is immediate danger to life
crisisPage.immediateDangerBody: Call your local emergency number (911 in the US, 999 in the UK, 112 in the EU) or go to the nearest emergency department.

insightsPage.title: Progress
insightsPage.subtitle: A short recap of how your weeks have actually been going.
insightsPage.firstRecapTitle: Your first recap is on its way
insightsPage.firstRecapBody: Once you've had a week of checking in, ticking off habits or trying an exercise, Kalm will write you a short recap of how it went — in plain language, with one small focus for the week ahead. Nothing to set up; it'll simply be here.
insightsPage.seeNumbersBody: Mood trends, habit grid and check-in scores, if you'd like the detail.

carePage.title: Talking to a person
carePage.subtitle: Kalm is here for the day-to-day, but there are things a trained human does better. These are places to start — no pressure, and no wrong time to use them.

groups.crisis: If things feel unsafe right now

exercisesPage.title: Guided exercises
exercisesPage.subtitle: These follow established protocols — thought records, behavioral activation, grounding, breathing and contained worry time. Nothing here is a treatment plan; use what helps.
